title: Letters from China & Japan

authors.name: L. D. S. [Lilias Dunlop Findlay Swainson]

summary: Forty-three letters home by an Englishwoman who in 1870 travelled out alone to join her husband, “H.”, a teacher of English and navigation to Chinese pupils at the Imperial Arsenal at Foochow. She went by Paris, Marseilles, Suez, Ceylon, and Singapore to Hong Kong, and lived about two and a half years at the Arsenal. The letters describe her house and servants, the French and English staff, the pupils, festivals, a typhoon, the news of the Tientsin massacre and the Franco-Prussian war, missions, and a house-boat trip up the Min. The last seven letters cover about six weeks in Japan late in 1872: Yokohama, Yedo, the new railway, and the Daibutsu at Kamakura.
The years, printed as “187-”, are inferred from events the letters mention. The title page names the author only as “L. D. S.”; the name is the library catalogue’s attribution.
omitted_from_reading: The half-title, the publisher’s advertisements and catalogue are in the JSON only.
notes_on_text: No contents are printed. The contents entries are the editor’s: the number of each letter with the place and date of its heading, or its main subject; the years, printed “187-”, are inferred from events the letters mention.
The engraved title page, the book’s only illustration, is placed at the start of the reading editions.
In the publisher’s catalogue at the end (in the JSON only), four letters of “narrative” did not print; they are supplied.

history.note: A printer’s error corrected: “pertorm” for “perform” (p. 46) (found by a sweep of all the books at the review after forty books).
A printer’s error of a dropped or transposed letter marked and corrected: “mavellous” for “marvellous”.
